questions.text: A particle of charge 1.6 µC and mass 16 µg is present in a strong magnetic field of 6.28 T. The particle is then fired perpendicular to magnetic field. The time required for the particle to return to original location for the first time is __________ s. (π = 3.14)
questions.sol_text: When a charged particle moves perpendicular to a magnetic field, it undergoes circular motion. The angular frequency is ω = qB/m. The period of one complete revolution is T = 2πm/(qB). Substituting values: T = (2 × 3.14 × 16 × 10^(-9))/(1.6 × 10^(-6) × 6.28) = (2 × 3.14 × 16 × 10^(-9))/(1.6 × 10^(-6) × 6.28) = 0.01 s

questions.text: In a moving coil galvanometer, two moving coils M₁ and M₂ have the following particulars: R₁ = 5Ω, N₁ = 15, A₁ = 3.6×10^(-3) m², B₁ = 0.25T; R₂ = 7Ω, N₂ = 21, A₂ = 1.8×10^(-3) m², B₂ = 0.50T. Assuming that torsional constant of the springs are same for both coils, what will be the ratio of voltage sensitivity of M₁ and M₂?
questions.sol_text: Voltage sensitivity of a moving coil galvanometer is S_v = (N × A × B)/(k × R), where k is the torsional constant of the spring. Since k is same for both coils, S_v ∝ (N × A × B)/R. For M₁: S_v1 ∝ (15 × 3.6×10^(-3) × 0.25)/5 = (15 × 3.6 × 0.25)/(5 × 10³) = 13.5/(5 × 10³). For M₂: S_v2 ∝ (21 × 1.8×10^(-3) × 0.50)/7 = (21 × 1.8 × 0.50)/(7 × 10³) = 18.9/(7 × 10³). Ratio = (13.5/5)/(18.9/7) = (13.5 × 7)/(5 × 18.9) = 94.5/94.5 = 1/1

questions.text: Let B_i be the magnitude of magnetic field at center of a circular coil of radius R carrying current I. Let B_x be the magnitude of magnetic field at an axial distance 'x' from the center. For x:R = 3:4, B_x/B_i is:
questions.sol_text: Magnetic field at center of coil: B_i = μ₀I/(2R). Magnetic field at axial distance x: B_x = μ₀IR²/[2(R² + x²)^(3/2)]. Ratio: B_x/B_i = R³/(R² + x²)^(3/2). Given x:R = 3:4, so x = 3k, R = 4k. Then R² + x² = 16k² + 9k² = 25k². B_x/B_i = (4k)³/(25k²)^(3/2) = 64k³/(125k³) = 64/125.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Given below are two statements; one is labeled as Assertion A and the other is labeled as Reason R. Assertion A: If oxygen ion (O^-2) and Hydrogen ion (H^+) enter normal to the magnetic field with equal momentum, then the path of O^-2 ion has a smaller curvature than that of H^+. Reason R: A proton with same linear momentum as an electron will form a path of smaller radius of curvature on entering a uniform magnetic field perpendicularly. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.sol_text: When a charged particle enters a magnetic field perpendicularly, radius of curvature r = p/(qB) where p is momentum, q is charge, B is magnetic field. For equal momentum: r is inversely proportional to charge. O^-2 has charge -2e, H^+ has charge +e. So r(O^-2) = p/(2eB) and r(H^+) = p/(eB). Thus r(O^-2) < r(H^+), meaning O^-2 has smaller radius of curvature. Assertion A is TRUE. For Reason R: comparing proton and electron with same momentum, proton has charge +e, electron has charge -e (same magnitude). Both would have same radius magnitude r = p/eB. Reason R is FALSE - they form paths of SAME radius, not different. Therefore A is true but R is false.

questions.text: A loop ABCDA, carrying current I=12 A, is placed in a plane consists of two semicircular segments of radius R₁ = 6π m and R₂ = 4π m. The magnitude of the resultant magnetic field at center O is k×10^(-7) T. The value of k is _____ (Given μ₀ = 4π×10^(-7) TmA^(-1))
questions.sol_text: For a semicircular current loop, magnetic field at center is B = (μ₀I)/(4R). The loop consists of two semicircles with radii R₁ = 6π m and R₂ = 4π m. Both semicircles have current flowing in the same direction (from A to D). Field due to semicircle with R₁: B₁ = (μ₀I)/(4R₁) = (4π×10^(-7)×12)/(4×6π) = (12×10^(-7))/6 = 2×10^(-7) T. Field due to semicircle with R₂: B₂ = (μ₀I)/(4R₂) = (4π×10^(-7)×12)/(4×4π) = (12×10^(-7))/4 = 3×10^(-7) T. Since both fields point in the same direction (perpendicular to the plane), resultant B = B₁ + B₂ = 2×10^(-7) + 3×10^(-7) = 5×10^(-7) T. Therefore k = 5.

questions.text: A current carrying is placed vertically and a particle of mass m with charge Q is released from rest. The particle moves along the axis of solenoid. If g is acceleration due to gravity then the acceleration (a) of the charged particle will satisfy:
questions.sol_text: Since the solenoid is placed vertically, the magnetic field inside the solenoid will be either along -y or +y axis. The particle will gain velocity along the -y axis (downward). questions.text: The current passing through a conducting loop in the form of equilateral triangle of side 4*sqrt(3) cm is 2A. The magnetic field at its centroid is alpha x 10^(-5) T. The value of alpha is ____. (Given: mu_0 = 4*pi x 10^(-7) SI units)
questions.sol_text:
For an equilateral triangle with side a = 4*sqrt(3) cm = 4*sqrt(3) x 10^(-2) m

The distance from centroid to each side is d = a/(2*sqrt(3)) = (4*sqrt(3))/(2*sqrt(3)) = 2 cm = 2 x 10^(-2) m

For an equilateral triangle, the centroid is equidistant from all three sides. Each side subtends equal angles at the centroid.

The magnetic field at the centroid due to one side of the triangle is:
B_side = (mu_0 * I)/(4*pi * d) * [sin(theta_1) + sin(theta_2)]

where theta_1 and theta_2 are the angles subtended by the ends of the side at the perpendicular from centroid.

For equilateral triangle, theta_1 = theta_2 = 60°

B_side = (mu_0 * I)/(4*pi * d) * [sin(60°) + sin(60°)]

Total magnetic field from all three sides:
B = (mu_0)/(4*pi) * (1/d) * [sin(60°) + sin(60°)] x 3

B = 10^(-7) * (2)/(2 x 10^(-2)) * (sqrt(3)/2 + sqrt(3)/2) x 3

B = 10^(-7) * (2)/(2 x 10^(-2)) * (sqrt(3)) x 3

B = sqrt(3) x 10^(-5) x 3

B = 3*sqrt(3) x 10^(-5) T

Therefore, alpha = 3*sqrt(3)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two identical circular loops P and Q each of radius r are lying in parallel planes such that they have common axis. The current through P and Q are I and 4I respectively in clockwise direction as seen from O. The net magnetic field at O is:
questions.sol_text:
B_net = B_1 - B_2

The magnetic field at the center of a circular loop of radius R carrying current i is:
B = mu_0*i/(2*R)

For loop P at distance R carrying current I:
B_1 = (mu_0*I*R^2)/(2*(R^2 + R^2)^(3/2)) = (mu_0*I*R^2)/(2*(2*R^2)^(3/2))

For loop Q at distance R carrying current 4I:
B_2 = (mu_0*4I*R^2)/(2*(R^2 + R^2)^(3/2)) = (4*mu_0*I*R^2)/(2*(2*R^2)^(3/2))

Simplifying:
B_1 = (mu_0*I*R^2)/(2*2^(3/2)*R^3) = (mu_0*I)/(2*2^(3/2)*R)

B_2 = (4*mu_0*I*R^2)/(2*2^(3/2)*R^3) = (4*mu_0*I)/(2*2^(3/2)*R) = (2*mu_0*I)/(2^(1/2)*R)

B_net = B_1 - B_2

Since the currents are in the same direction (both clockwise from O), and B_2 > B_1, the net field points toward Q.

B_net = (4*mu_0*I*R^2)/(2*(R^2 + R^2)^(3/2)) - (mu_0*I*R^2)/(2*(R^2 + R^2)^(3/2))

= (3*mu_0*I*R^2)/(2*(2*R^2)^(3/2))

= (3*mu_0*I)/(4*sqrt(2)*R)

Direction: towards Q (since B_2 > B_1)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A long cylindrical conductor with large cross section carries an electric current distributed uniformly over its cross-section. Magnetic field due to this current is:
options: maximum at either ends of the conductor and minimum at the midpoint
maximum at the axis of the conductor
minimum at the surface of the conductor
minimum at the axis of the conductor
questions.sol_text:
For a solid cylinder carrying uniformly distributed current:

Using Ampere's law in cylindrical coordinates, the magnetic field at a distance r from the axis is:

Inside the conductor (r < R, where R is radius):
B(r) = (mu_0 * I * r)/(2 * pi * R^2)

At the axis (r = 0):
B = 0 (minimum)

At the surface (r = R):
B = (mu_0 * I)/(2 * pi * R) (maximum)

Outside the conductor (r > R):
B(r) = (mu_0 * I)/(2 * pi * r)

The magnetic field increases linearly from the axis to the surface and then decreases as 1/r outside.

Therefore:
- B_min at the axis of the conductor (at r = 0, B = 0)
- B_max at the surface of the conductor (at r = R)

The graph shows B vs r with maximum at the surface and minimum at the axis.

Correct statement: D Only - minimum at the axis of the conductor

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Three long straight wires carrying current are arranged mutually parallel as shown in the figure. The force experienced by 15 cm length of wire Q is ____ . (μ_0 = 4π × 10^(-7) T·m / A )
questions.sol_text:
F_net = (μ_0 / 2π) I_0 (I_1 / d_1 + I_2 / d_2) ℓ

F_net = 2 × 10^(-7) × 1 × (3/3 + 2/2) × (15 × 10^(-2)) / 10^(-2)

= 4 × 15 × 10^(-7)

F_net = 6 × 10^(-6) N

Since wire Q carries current downward (1A), wire P carries current upward (3A), and wire R carries current downward (2A):
- Force between Q and P: opposite currents (upward force on Q towards P, but repulsive, so away from P)
- Force between Q and R: same direction currents (attractive, towards R)

Net force is towards R with magnitude 6 × 10^(-6) N

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying circular loop of radius R is 16μ T. The magnetic field at a distance x = sqrt(3)R on its axis from the centre is ____ μT.
questions.sol_text:
The magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying circular loop is given by:
B_centre = μ₀I/(2R) = 16μ T

The magnetic field at a distance x on the axis of the loop is given by:
B_x = μ₀IR²/[2(x² + R²)^(3/2)]

Substituting x = sqrt(3)R:
B_x = μ₀IR²/[2((sqrt(3)R)² + R²)^(3/2)]
     = μ₀IR²/[2(3R² + R²)^(3/2)]
     = μ₀IR²/[2(4R²)^(3/2)]
     = μ₀IR²/(2 × 8R³)
     = μ₀I/(16R)
     = (1/8) × μ₀I/(2R)
     = (1/8) × 16μ T
     = 2μ T
